name: WebGuard Security Lab
release_status: expanded-tool-center-integrated; external engines disabled by default; frontend build and Docker deployment require final environment validation

features: AI Copilot UI with local/remote mode status
tool catalog/status based on fresh worker heartbeat
Tool Center for queued scans and source-code security scans
local rules fallback for process review, audit summaries, finding triage and remediation
AI endpoint authorization, rate limiting, secret redaction and usage audit events
bounded allow-listed adapters for headers/DNS/TLS/auth surface, ZAP passive, Nuclei, Schemathesis, k6, Playwright/accessibility, Trivy, Semgrep, Gitleaks, testssl.sh and CycloneDX SBOM
audit-event history and run regression comparison

security_boundary.integration_status: used by built-in network adapters; external CLI/browser adapters still require deployment-level egress filtering due to DNS check/use limitations

features: optional worker Compose profile with a dedicated Playwright/Chromium and Python-engine image
worker capability heartbeat; production refuses new jobs when worker heartbeat is stale
external engine safety flags and catalog readiness

ai_copilot.provider: Groq OpenAI-compatible chat-completions API configured server-side (default model: openai/gpt-oss-120b)
ai_copilot.fallback: Local deterministic rules when a model is not configured or temporarily unavailable
ai_copilot.security: Advisory only; no tools or scan execution; output and user inputs are treated as untrusted

features: authorization check before execution and while running
workspace scans limited to server-configured root
tool_center.critical_gate: external tools require tested deployment egress filtering; Compose network alone is not an egress firewall

notes: Never commit secrets, .env.production, databases, node_modules, virtual environments, build caches, or backup files.
All network assessments require explicit authorization for targets and paths.
External CLI/browser engines remain disabled by default. Missing dependencies must remain unavailable in the catalog.
A config flag is not a firewall: enforce and test worker egress filtering before enabling external engines.
Queue coordination and rate limits are single-worker/process-local and must be upgraded before horizontal scale.
Accessibility findings are heuristics, not WCAG certification; reported regression resolution means no longer observed, not proven fixed.
The Groq AI Copilot remains advisory-only and cannot launch scans or modify scope.
Tool Center release 0.9.0: database-persisted worker heartbeat, fail-closed production behavior when worker is stale/offline, bounded adapters and export/regression features.

The dedicated worker image currently bundles pinned Python integrations and Chromium; native CLI binaries (Nuclei, k6, Trivy, Gitleaks, testssl.sh) are not bundled and remain unavailable unless added from verified vendor releases.
Docker Compose networks do not enforce destination-aware egress policy; external engines must remain disabled until independently enforced and tested network filtering is in place.
